about.title: About Dividend Calculator - Stock Dividend Income Analysis Tool
about.description: The Dividend Calculator is an investment analysis tool designed to help investors estimate dividend income, yields, and growth projections from dividend-paying stocks. Whether you're evaluating individual stocks, building a dividend portfolio, or planning retirement income, this calculator provides formula-based projections for dividend payments, reinvestment scenarios, and total returns. It can help you review income-focused investing scenarios and long-term growth assumptions.

howTo.title: How to Use the Dividend Calculator

steps.title: Stock Information
steps.description: Enter the stock symbol, current price, and number of shares you own or plan to purchase.

steps.title: Dividend Details
steps.description: Input the annual dividend per share and dividend payment frequency (quarterly, monthly, etc.).

steps.title: Dividend Growth Rate
steps.description: Enter the expected annual dividend growth rate based on company history and projections.

steps.title: Investment Timeline
steps.description: Specify your investment holding period for long-term dividend growth calculations.

steps.title: Reinvestment Options
steps.description: Choose whether to reinvest dividends (DRIP) or receive cash payments.

steps.title: Analyze Returns
steps.description: Review dividend yield, annual income, total return projections, and compound growth scenarios.

faq.q: What's a good dividend yield for stocks?
faq.a: Dividend yields typically range from 1-6%. High-quality dividend stocks often yield 2-4%, while REITs and utilities may yield 4-8%. Be cautious of yields above 8% as they may indicate financial distress or unsustainable payouts.

faq.q: Should I reinvest dividends or take cash?
faq.a: Dividend reinvestment (DRIP) compounds your returns over time and may suit long-term growth goals. Taking cash may fit better if you need current income or want to rebalance your portfolio. Consider your investment timeline and income needs.

Qualified dividends from US companies are taxed at capital gains rates (0%, 15%, or 20%). Non-qualified dividends are taxed as ordinary income. Hold stocks for 60+ days around ex-dividend date to qualify for preferential tax treatment.

faq.q: What's the difference between dividend yield and total return?
faq.a: Dividend yield is annual dividends divided by stock price. Total return includes both dividend income and capital appreciation (or depreciation). Focus on total return for complete investment performance analysis.
